# contentful_app_signing_secret (Resource)

Manages a Contentful App Signing Secret.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# This example also uses the hashicorp/random provider to generate the secret.
resource "contentful_app_signing_secret" "this" {
  organization_id   = var.contentful_organization_id
  app_definition_id = var.app_definition_id

  value = random_password.contentful_app_signing_secret.result
}

resource "random_password" "contentful_app_signing_secret" {
  override_special = "+/=_-"

  length = 64
}
```

## Write-only signing secret

With Terraform 1.11.1 or later, use `value_wo` and an ephemeral variable to keep the
complete secret out of this resource's plan and state. Use this example as an
alternative to the ordinary `value` example above:

```terraform
variable "signing_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

resource "contentful_app_signing_secret" "this" {
  organization_id   = var.contentful_organization_id
  app_definition_id = var.app_definition_id

  value_wo = var.signing_secret
}
```

Changing from `value` to `value_wo` with exactly the same secret removes the
complete value from new state without rotating the secret. Historical state
snapshots can still contain it. See [migrating signing-secret values](../guides/secrets-and-state#migrating-signing-secret-values)
and [planning rotations](../guides/secrets-and-state#planning-and-rotating-write-only-signing-secrets).

Use cryptographically generated secrets and protect Terraform state and backups.
See [secret protection](../guides/secrets-and-state#write-only-signing-secrets) and
[mutation failures and recovery](../guides/secrets-and-state#recovering-an-uncertain-signing-secret-write).

## Schema

### Required

- `app_definition_id` (String) ID of the app definition for which the signing secret is created. Changing this value replaces the resource.
- `organization_id` (String) ID of the organization that owns the app. Changing this value replaces the resource.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `value` (String, Sensitive) Symmetric key shared between Contentful and an app backend. Must be exactly 64 characters matching `^[0-9a-zA-Z+/=_-]+$`. Exactly one of `value` and `value_wo` is required. Stored in Terraform state. Import leaves `value` null; applying the configured value can rotate the secret. Timeout-only updates preserve the secret and stored value. See [importing signing secrets](../guides/secrets-and-state#importing-signing-secrets).
- `value_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only signing secret, with the same format as `value`. Configure exactly one of `value` and `value_wo`. Requires Terraform 1.11.1 or later and accepts ephemeral values. The complete value is excluded from this resource's plan and state. Every update compares the supplied value, including timeout-only updates; a different value can rotate the secret even with `ignore_changes = [value_wo]`. See [write-only signing secrets](../guides/secrets-and-state#write-only-signing-secrets) for rotation and saved-plan behavior.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Contentful creation timestamp in RFC 3339 format, or null when omitted. It can change when the signing secret is replaced. Write-only updates can make this unknown during planning and trigger downstream replacement even without a secret write.
- `id` (String) Composite Terraform resource identifier in `organization_id/app_definition_id` form.
- `updated_at` (String) Contentful update timestamp in RFC 3339 format, or null when omitted. Write-only updates can make this unknown during planning and trigger downstream replacement even without a secret write.

## Import

~> Import leaves `value` null. Applying the configured value can replace the remote secret, including during a configuration-driven import. See [importing signing secrets](../guides/secrets-and-state#importing-signing-secrets).

Choose one of the following methods. Match the resource address and Contentful IDs to your configuration, then review the plan before applying.

### Import by identity

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) with `identity`:

```terraform
import {
  identity = {
    organization_id   = var.contentful_organization_id
    app_definition_id = var.app_definition_id
  }
  to = contentful_app_signing_secret.this
}
```

### Import by ID

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) with `id`:

```terraform
import {
  id = "${var.contentful_organization_id}/${var.app_definition_id}"
  to = contentful_app_signing_secret.this
}
```

### Import with the CLI

Use the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import). Set the shell variables to your Contentful IDs before running it:

```shell
terraform import contentful_app_signing_secret.this "$CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID/$CONTENTFUL_APP_DEFINITION_ID"
```
